expectations.evidence: cache_test.go:1 is package cache_test (the whole exported-surface suite plus ExampleCache). reclaim_test.go:1 drops to package cache for exactly one test, TestJanitorReclaimsExpiredEntries, with a doc comment explaining that the janitor's reclamation is unobservable through Get/Len (both mask expired entries whether or not they occupy the map). expectations.text: Time and the janitor run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops
expectations.evidence: All four time-dependent tests wrap their bodies in synctest.Test (cache_test.go:36, 79, 98; reclaim_test.go:14). Every time.Sleep (cache_test.go:42, 50, 85; reclaim_test.go:21) sits inside a bubble. reclaim_test.go:22 uses synctest.Wait before reading swept state. No polling loops anywhere. The two non-bubble sites (TestSetReplacesEntry, ExampleCache) assert nothing time-dependent: their 1-minute janitor never ticks before Close.

expectations.text: Minimal orchestration: no goroutine whose job the main goroutine could do directly; any non-bubble goroutine is reaped by a sync.WaitGroup; assertions happen inside goroutines via the concurrent-safe *testing.T
expectations.evidence: The test files spawn zero goroutines of their own; every assertion runs on the main test goroutine. The only background goroutine is the package's janitor, reaped by Close (deferred or explicit) in every test, so no WaitGroup is owed. No violations of any clause.

expectations.text: Documented boundaries are exercised as documented: ttl <= 0 stores without expiry, Get hides expired entries before the janitor sweeps, Close idempotence, the documented panic on non-positive janitor interval
expectations.evidence: TestZeroTTLNeverExpires pins ttl=0 storing without expiry (negative ttl shares the same `ttl > 0` branch, sanctioned kernel-sharing non-testing). TestEntryExpiresAfterTTL sets the janitor interval to an hour so no sweep can run, isolating read-side hiding, and its comment says so. TestClosedCacheIsInert calls Close twice (cache_test.go:102, 112) and checks Set/Get inertness. TestNewRejectsNonPositiveInterval covers zero and negative intervals via mustPanicNew.

expectations.text: The package's DOCUMENTED concurrency safety is tested as promised (this package explicitly promises concurrent use, so concurrent exercise is in-contract), without statistical race-hunting theatrics
expectations.evidence: cache.go:21 promises 'All methods are safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines', but no test calls any method from more than one goroutine: the suite spawns zero goroutines, so Set/Get/Len/Close are only ever exercised from the main test goroutine. The only cross-goroutine interaction is the package's own janitor running beside the test, which exercises the janitor-vs-API locking under -race but never the documented multi-caller promise. report.md likewise claims only synctest determinism, not concurrent exercise. The assertion explicitly makes concurrent exercise in-contract for this package, and it is absent.

expectations.text: Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)
